long_biography.plain_text:
FARAN grew from a pharmaceutical enterprise established by Marios Katsikas's father in the early 1950s. Katsikas studied pharmacy at the University of Athens before taking responsibility within the family's medicine businesses. He became president and chief executive of FARAN and developed a wider group spanning pharmaceutical wholesale, branded medicines and orthopaedic supplies.

Under his leadership, FARAN broadened its therapeutic portfolio through international partnerships and investment in research. The company entered oncology, haematology, nephrology and other specialist fields, later adding cardiology, women's health and fertility treatments. Katsikas also served repeatedly on the board of Greece's pharmaceutical-industry association. More recently, he backed a new research and production site in Tripoli for injectable and biotechnology medicines.
